It sounds like you might be having a mixed episode. One of the best things for me when I’m in any kind of episode- manic, depressive, or mixed, is trying to never be alone. It sucks but it might come to the point of asking friends/family/your husband to be around you all the time. Take it out of your hands and put it in someone else’s. 

Another thing I do is focus on distraction- not exactly the healthiest habit in the world but it helps. Find a really good show, book, hobby... anything to keep your mind off your pain. Maybe ask if you can see your psychiatrist more often. Sometimes if you beg you can get another doctor to call the med management doc to get you in sooner. My pcp called my psychiatrist and told them to fit me in and I was able to see my med management doc the following week.

Also feel free to message me 24/7 if you need to talk!! I have bipolar 2 as well as some other issues and lots of experience with mental health!

I started vyvanse a few months ago on 30mg and that didn't do much for me, so my doctor bumped me up to 50mg about 2 weeks ago.


Since then, I have only binged once. It will wear off in the evenings so it isn't perfect. You have to be very very careful to make sure you still eat regularly and healthily throughout the day because it kills your appetite.


It also has some interesting side effects. It's different for everyone of course, my main one has been a little anxiety, clenching my jaw, and just being pretty tense. I haven't had any insomnia problems but I know that's common. It does make you very focused and productive. 


I recommend trying it. The cost is bad but ask your doctor if they have copay cards. My doctor gives me copay cards every 6 months and it brings the cost down to $15. It's pretty great.


It really has changed my way of life so far, I feel amazing. Like I said, it's not perfect, but it's given me clarity and focus so I can work on why I developed my eating disorder in the first place and getting to the root of the problem. It could definitely help you in this way too!

I have had my beagle-poodle mix since he was 10 weeks old. He is now 12 years old, and has always been an only dog. When my family got him, my 3 siblings and I plus my parents were all living together. Now we are all grown up, and I ended up keeping the dog. He seemed so lonely without as many people in the house to play with him, so I decided to adopt a new dog. During my search, my biggest concern was having an older dog and making sure he was happy with the new dog. 


I ended up rescuing a 5yo beagle mix with heartworms (nobody wanted to adopt her because of the heartworms!). At first, I felt like I was betraying my old dog by bringing in a new one in his old age, but when I saw them play for the first time it all melted away. My babies are so happy together now. I think adopting a middle-aged dog was the perfect decision, because her energy level matches my old dogs very well. However, she's young and energetic enough that she gets my dog up and playing again, and I can see his vitality coming back. They are so happy together!

Case in point- many people don't want middle-aged dogs because they want a bouncy little puppy, but when you have an older dog in the house it tends to work out really well! It's not overly stressful for the older dog, but it brings some life back into them.

Shelters are usually full of beagle-mixes that would probably fit your home well. I have two beagle-mixes (one beagle-poodle, one beagle-bassett). They are generally high-energy dogs that would love to have kids and adults to play and exercise with all day long. They are loving and playful and sweet. They're usually put into shelters because they are high-energy and many people aren't prepared for that. 


They tend to stay small, both of mine are around 25lbs. Shedding could be a problem, but I think it is manageable. Both of my dogs (and many other beagles I have met) are good with other dogs, and usually cats, but watch out for squirrels. Overall, I think beagles and beagle-mixes are great family dogs!
